svg.title: Pareto front: cost against CO₂, solved by ε-constraint
svg.desc: Bi-objective design trade-off, both objectives minimised: total annualised cost c in M€/a (horizontal) against CO₂ emissions e in kt/a (vertical). The attainable set is bounded by the convex frontier e = -4 + 434/(c − 8.5) for c from 12 to 24. 11 efficient designs lie on it, evenly spaced along the drawn curve; 210 seeded candidate designs (small dots) lie above it inside the ideal–nadir box. A non-dominated filter over all 221 designs returns exactly the 11 efficient designs (round markers on the 2-unit Pareto front); every small dot is dominated by at least one of them. Axis ticks: cost 12 to 24 M€/a in steps of 3, CO₂ at 50, 75, 100 and 120 kt/a. Utopia point (12, 24) and nadir point (24, 120) span the dashed box. Dashed ε-lines show the ε-constraint method, min c subject to e ≤ ε, at ε = 89.27, 62.42, 43.18, 31.35 kt/a; each touches the front at its optimum, c = 13.15, 15.03, 17.7, 20.78 M€/a, where the constraint is active. The hatched quadrant is the region dominated by design A (15.03, 62.42). Inset: design A against design B (20.78, 31.35) as pixel bars, cost and CO₂, each metric on its own zero-based scale.
